"""Write the per-employer CSV and the employer's sections of the audit report and questions."""

from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import io
import re
from decimal import Decimal
from pathlib import Path

from allocate import ZERO, Result

CSV_HEADER = ["class_code", "payroll_allocated", "rationale_ref"]

REPORT_TITLE = """# Audit report: class codes and payroll allocation

First-pass classification by the class-code-assistant Skill. Amounts are US dollars for each employer's audit period.
The Skill classifies and allocates payroll only; it does not set rates or quote premium. Each section says whether the
employer's own split is accepted, every adjustment with its amount, and the records that decided it. Paragraph
identifiers (CG-nn) are cited from the classification guide read during the run.
"""

QUESTIONS_TITLE = """# Audit questions for the employers

Questions for the premium auditor to put to each employer before signing off. Each one names the employee,
subcontractor or record it is about. Every adjustment and every record the allocation relies on is covered by at least
one question.
"""


def codes_csv(result: Result) -> str:
    buf = io.StringIO()
    w = csv.writer(buf, lineterminator="\n")
    w.writerow(CSV_HEADER)
    for code, amount, ref in result.lines():
        w.writerow([code, f"{amount:.2f}", ref])
    return buf.getvalue()


def _md(text: str) -> str:
    return text.replace("|", "\\|")


def _decision(r: Result) -> str:
    reg = r.employer.record_files["payroll_register"]
    if r.accepted:
        others = [f for f in r.records_used if f not in (reg, "field-notes.md")]
        checked = f", checked against {', '.join(others)}" if others else ""
        return (f"**Decision: the employer's own split is accepted.** The payroll register ({reg}) gives the same codes and "
                f"amounts to the cent{checked}, and no record shows payroll that can be measured under another code.")
    files = []
    for a in r.adjustments:
        for f in a.records:
            if f not in files:
                files.append(f)
    return (f"**Decision: the employer's own split is not accepted.** The employer's records disagree with the application, "
            f"and the records decide. The allocation rests on {', '.join(files)}.")


def report_section(r: Result) -> str:
    e = r.employer
    out = [f"## {e.name}", ""]
    files = ["application.md", "business-description.md"]
    if e.field_notes:
        files.append("field-notes.md")
    files += [f for f in e.record_files.values()]
    out.append(f"Application {e.application_id}. Audit period {e.period_start} to {e.period_end}. Classification guide "
               f"edition {r.guide.edition}. Employer file read: {', '.join(files)}.")
    if e.unused_files:
        out.append("Not used for the allocation: " + "; ".join(f"{k} ({v})" for k, v in e.unused_files.items()) + ".")
    out += ["", _decision(r), "", "### Codes and payroll allocated", "",
            "| Class code | Payroll allocated | Rationale ref | Code described as |", "|---|---:|---|---|"]
    total = ZERO
    for code, amount, ref in r.lines():
        out.append(f"| {code} | {amount:.2f} | {ref} | {r.guide.code_paragraph(code).code_name} |")
        total += amount
    out += [f"| Total | {total:.2f} | | |", "", f"Principal business code: {r.governing_code}; {r.governing_basis}.", ""]

    out += ["### Compared with the employer's own split", "",
            "| Class code | Employer reported | Allocated | Difference |", "|---|---:|---:|---:|"]
    reported, alloc = r.reported, r.by_code
    rep_total = ZERO
    for code in [c for c in r.guide.codes if c in reported or c in alloc]:
        rv, av = reported.get(code, ZERO), alloc.get(code, ZERO)
        rep_total += rv
        out.append(f"| {code} | {rv:.2f} | {av:.2f} | {av - rv:+.2f} |")
    out += [f"| Total | {rep_total:.2f} | {total:.2f} | {total - rep_total:+.2f} |", ""]
    if e.employer_note:
        out += [f"Employer's note on the application: \"{e.employer_note}\"", ""]
    if r.employer_assignment:
        names = {s.key: s.label for s in r.subjects}
        per_code: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
        for eid, code in r.employer_assignment.items():
            per_code.setdefault(code, []).append(names[eid])
        out.append("The employer's figures match these employees on the register: "
                   + "; ".join(f"{c}: {', '.join(n)}" for c, n in per_code.items()) + ".")
        out.append("")
    if not r.accepted:
        out.append("Where and why the allocation differs:")
        out.append("")
        for code in [c for c in r.guide.codes if c in reported or c in alloc]:
            diff = alloc.get(code, ZERO) - reported.get(code, ZERO)
            if diff:
                ins = [a for a in r.adjustments if a.to_code == code]
                outs = [a for a in r.adjustments if a.from_code == code]
                parts = []
                if ins:
                    parts.append("in: " + "; ".join(f"{a.subject} {a.amount:.2f}" for a in ins))
                if outs:
                    parts.append("out: " + "; ".join(f"{a.subject} {a.amount:.2f}" for a in outs))
                out.append(f"- {code} {diff:+.2f} ({' | '.join(parts)})")
        out.append("")

    out += ["### Adjustments", ""]
    if r.adjustments:
        out += ["| # | Employee or payment | Amount | From | To | Why | Records | Guide |", "|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|---|"]
        for i, a in enumerate(r.adjustments, 1):
            out.append(f"| {i} | {_md(a.subject)} | {a.amount:.2f} | {a.from_code or 'not reported'} | {a.to_code or 'not counted'} | "
                       f"{_md(a.reason)} | {', '.join(a.records)} | {', '.join(a.refs)} |")
    else:
        out.append("None. Every employee's payroll stays under the code the employer reported.")
    out.append("")
    if r.excluded:
        out += ["### Paid but not counted as payroll", "", "| Employee or payment | Amount | Why |", "|---|---:|---|"]
        for who, amount, why in r.excluded:
            out.append(f"| {_md(who)} | {amount:.2f} | {_md(why)} |")
        out.append("")

    out += ["### Allocation by employee and payment", "", "| Employee or payment | Class code | Amount | Basis | Records |", "|---|---|---:|---|---|"]
    for s in r.subjects:
        for p in s.portions:
            out.append(f"| {_md(s.label)} | {p.code} | {p.amount:.2f} | {_md(p.basis)} | {', '.join(p.records)} |")
    out += ["", "### Records that decided this file", ""]
    for f, what in r.records_used.items():
        out.append(f"- {f}: {what}.")
    out.append("")
    if r.assumptions:
        out += ["### Assumptions where the guide is silent", ""]
        out += [f"- {a}" for a in r.assumptions]
        out.append("")
    if r.notes:
        out += ["### Notes", ""]
        out += [f"- {n}" for n in r.notes]
        out.append("")
    return "\n".join(out).rstrip() + "\n"


def questions_section(r: Result) -> str:
    out = [f"## {r.employer.name}", ""]
    for i, q in enumerate(r.questions, 1):
        out.append(f"{i}. **{q.subject}.** {q.text}")
    return "\n".join(out) + "\n"


SECTION_RE = re.compile(r"<!-- BEGIN employer:(?P<slug>[a-z0-9-]+) -->\n(?P<body>.*?)<!-- END employer:(?P=slug) -->\n", re.S)


def merge_sections(path: Path, title: str, slug: str, body: str, order: list[str]) -> None:
    """Insert or replace one employer's section; keep sections in the configured order."""
    sections: dict[str, str] = {}
    if path.exists():
        for m in SECTION_RE.finditer(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")):
            sections[m.group("slug")] = m.group("body")
    sections[slug] = body
    ranked = sorted(sections, key=lambda s: (order.index(s) if s in order else len(order), s))
    parts = [title]
    for s in ranked:
        parts.append(f"<!-- BEGIN employer:{s} -->\n{sections[s]}<!-- END employer:{s} -->\n")
    path.write_text("\n".join(parts), encoding="utf-8")


def run_record(r: Result, sources: dict) -> dict:
    def d(x: Decimal) -> str:
        return f"{x:.2f}"

    return {
        "employer": r.employer.slug,
        "name": r.employer.name,
        "application": r.employer.application_id,
        "audit_period": [str(r.employer.period_start), str(r.employer.period_end)],
        "guide_edition": r.guide.edition,
        "sources": sources,
        "accepted_employer_split": r.accepted,
        "reported": {c: d(v) for c, v in r.reported.items()},
        "allocated": [{"class_code": c, "payroll_allocated": d(a), "rationale_ref": ref} for c, a, ref in r.lines()],
        "principal_business_code": r.governing_code,
        "subjects": [
            {"label": s.label, "kind": s.kind, "employer_code": s.employer_code,
             "portions": [{"code": p.code, "amount": d(p.amount), "basis": p.basis, "records": p.records, "refs": p.refs} for p in s.portions]}
            for s in r.subjects
        ],
        "excluded": [{"label": w, "amount": d(a), "why": y} for w, a, y in r.excluded],
        "adjustments": [{"subject": a.subject, "amount": d(a.amount), "from": a.from_code, "to": a.to_code, "reason": a.reason, "records": a.records, "refs": a.refs} for a in r.adjustments],
        "questions": [{"subject": q.subject, "text": q.text} for q in r.questions],
        "assumptions": r.assumptions,
        "records_used": r.records_used,
    }

Questions for the premium auditor to put to each employer before signing off. Each one names the employee,
subcontractor or record it is about. Every adjustment and every record the allocation relies on is covered by at least
one question.
"""


def codes_csv(result: Result) -> str:
    buf = io.StringIO()
    w = csv.writer(buf, lineterminator="\n")
    w.writerow(CSV_HEADER)
    for code, amount, ref in result.lines():
        w.writerow([code, f"{amount:.2f}", ref])
    return buf.getvalue()


def _md(text: str) -> str:
    return text.replace("|", "\\|")


def _decision(r: Result) -> str:
    reg = r.employer.record_files["payroll_register"]
    if r.accepted:
        others = [f for f in r.records_used if f not in (reg, "field-notes.md")]
        checked = f", checked against {', '.join(others)}" if others else ""
        return (f"**Decision: the employer's own split is accepted.** The payroll register ({reg}) gives the same codes and "
                f"amounts to the cent{checked}, and no record shows payroll that can be measured under another code.")
    files = []
    for a in r.adjustments:
        for f in a.records:
            if f not in files:
                files.append(f)
    return (f"**Decision: the employer's own split is not accepted.** The employer's records disagree with the application, "
            f"and the records decide. The allocation rests on {', '.join(files)}.")


def report_section(r: Result) -> str:
    e = r.employer
    out = [f"## {e.name}", ""]
    files = ["application.md", "business-description.md"]
    if e.field_notes:
        files.append("field-notes.md")
    files += [f for f in e.record_files.values()]
    out.append(f"Application {e.application_id}. Audit period {e.period_start} to {e.period_end}. Classification guide "
               f"edition {r.guide.edition}. Employer file read: {', '.join(files)}.")
    if e.unused_files:
        out.append("Not used for the allocation: " + "; ".join(f"{k} ({v})" for k, v in e.unused_files.items()) + ".")
    out += ["", _decision(r), "", "### Codes and payroll allocated", "",
            "| Class code | Payroll allocated | Rationale ref | Code described as |", "|---|---:|---|---|"]
    total = ZERO
    for code, amount, ref in r.lines():
        out.append(f"| {code} | {amount:.2f} | {ref} | {r.guide.code_paragraph(code).code_name} |")
        total += amount
    out += [f"| Total | {total:.2f} | | |", "", f"Principal business code: {r.governing_code}; {r.governing_basis}.", ""]

    out += ["### Compared with the employer's own split", "",
            "| Class code | Employer reported | Allocated | Difference |", "|---|---:|---:|---:|"]
    reported, alloc = r.reported, r.by_code
    rep_total = ZERO
    for code in [c for c in r.guide.codes if c in reported or c in alloc]:
        rv, av = reported.get(code, ZERO), alloc.get(code, ZERO)
        rep_total += rv
        out.append(f"| {code} | {rv:.2f} | {av:.2f} | {av - rv:+.2f} |")
    out += [f"| Total | {rep_total:.2f} | {total:.2f} | {total - rep_total:+.2f} |", ""]
    if e.employer_note:
        out += [f"Employer's note on the application: \"{e.employer_note}\"", ""]
    if r.employer_assignment:
        names = {s.key: s.label for s in r.subjects}
        per_code: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
        for eid, code in r.employer_assignment.items():
            per_code.setdefault(code, []).append(names[eid])
        out.append("The employer's figures match these employees on the register: "
                   + "; ".join(f"{c}: {', '.join(n)}" for c, n in per_code.items()) + ".")
        out.append("")
    if not r.accepted:
        out.append("Where and why the allocation differs:")
        out.append("")
        for code in [c for c in r.guide.codes if c in reported or c in alloc]:
            diff = alloc.get(code, ZERO) - reported.get(code, ZERO)
            if diff:
                ins = [a for a in r.adjustments if a.to_code == code]
                outs = [a for a in r.adjustments if a.from_code == code]
                parts = []
                if ins:
                    parts.append("in: " + "; ".join(f"{a.subject} {a.amount:.2f}" for a in ins))
                if outs:
                    parts.append("out: " + "; ".join(f"{a.subject} {a.amount:.2f}" for a in outs))
                out.append(f"- {code} {diff:+.2f} ({' | '.join(parts)})")
        out.append("")

    out += ["### Adjustments", ""]
    if r.adjustments:
        out += ["| # | Employee or payment | Amount | From | To | Why | Records | Guide |", "|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|---|"]
        for i, a in enumerate(r.adjustments, 1):
            out.append(f"| {i} | {_md(a.subject)} | {a.amount:.2f} | {a.from_code or 'not reported'} | {a.to_code or 'not counted'} | "
                       f"{_md(a.reason)} | {', '.join(a.records)} | {', '.join(a.refs)} |")
    else:
        out.append("None. Every employee's payroll stays under the code the employer reported.")
    out.append("")
    if r.excluded:
        out += ["### Paid but not counted as payroll", "", "| Employee or payment | Amount | Why |", "|---|---:|---|"]
        for who, amount, why in r.excluded:
            out.append(f"| {_md(who)} | {amount:.2f} | {_md(why)} |")
        out.append("")

    out += ["### Allocation by employee and payment", "", "| Employee or payment | Class code | Amount | Basis | Records |", "|---|---|---:|---|---|"]
    for s in r.subjects:
        for p in s.portions:
            out.append(f"| {_md(s.label)} | {p.code} | {p.amount:.2f} | {_md(p.basis)} | {', '.join(p.records)} |")
    out += ["", "### Records that decided this file", ""]
    for f, what in r.records_used.items():
        out.append(f"- {f}: {what}.")
    out.append("")
    if r.assumptions:
        out += ["### Assumptions where the guide is silent", ""]
        out += [f"- {a}" for a in r.assumptions]
        out.append("")
    if r.notes:
        out += ["### Notes", ""]
        out += [f"- {n}" for n in r.notes]
        out.append("")
    return "\n".join(out).rstrip() + "\n"


def questions_section(r: Result) -> str:
    out = [f"## {r.employer.name}", ""]
    for i, q in enumerate(r.questions, 1):
        out.append(f"{i}. **{q.subject}.** {q.text}")
    return "\n".join(out) + "\n"


SECTION_RE = re.compile(r"<!-- BEGIN employer:(?P<slug>[a-z0-9-]+) -->\n(?P<body>.*?)<!-- END employer:(?P=slug) -->\n", re.S)


def merge_sections(path: Path, title: str, slug: str, body: str, order: list[str]) -> None:
    """Insert or replace one employer's section; keep sections in the configured order."""
    sections: dict[str, str] = {}
    if path.exists():
        for m in SECTION_RE.finditer(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")):
            sections[m.group("slug")] = m.group("body")
    sections[slug] = body
    ranked = sorted(sections, key=lambda s: (order.index(s) if s in order else len(order), s))
    parts = [title]
    for s in ranked:
        parts.append(f"<!-- BEGIN employer:{s} -->\n{sections[s]}<!-- END employer:{s} -->\n")
    path.write_text("\n".join(parts), encoding="utf-8")


def run_record(r: Result, sources: dict) -> dict:
    def d(x: Decimal) -> str:
        return f"{x:.2f}"

    return {
        "employer": r.employer.slug,
        "name": r.employer.name,
        "application": r.employer.application_id,
        "audit_period": [str(r.employer.period_start), str(r.employer.period_end)],
        "guide_edition": r.guide.edition,
        "sources": sources,
        "accepted_employer_split": r.accepted,
        "reported": {c: d(v) for c, v in r.reported.items()},
        "allocated": [{"class_code": c, "payroll_allocated": d(a), "rationale_ref": ref} for c, a, ref in r.lines()],
        "principal_business_code": r.governing_code,
        "subjects": [
            {"label": s.label, "kind": s.kind, "employer_code": s.employer_code,
             "portions": [{"code": p.code, "amount": d(p.amount), "basis": p.basis, "records": p.records, "refs": p.refs} for p in s.portions]}
            for s in r.subjects
        ],
        "excluded": [{"label": w, "amount": d(a), "why": y} for w, a, y in r.excluded],
        "adjustments": [{"subject": a.subject, "amount": d(a.amount), "from": a.from_code, "to": a.to_code, "reason": a.reason, "records": a.records, "refs": a.refs} for a in r.adjustments],
        "questions": [{"subject": q.subject, "text": q.text} for q in r.questions],
        "assumptions": r.assumptions,
        "records_used": r.records_used,
    }

"""Run the class-code assistant on one or more employer files.

Reads the classification guide and the employer files from the audit team's Drive
folder at the start of every run (or from a local copy given with --source-dir),
then writes, per employer:

    deliverables/codes/<employer>.csv
    deliverables/audit-report.md      (the employer's section)
    deliverables/audit-questions.md   (the employer's section)
    runs/<employer>.json              (run record: sources read, allocation, questions)

Examples:
    python3 skills/class-code-assistant/scripts/run_audit.py --employer harbor-point-legal
    python3 skills/class-code-assistant/scripts/run_audit.py --all
    python3 skills/class-code-assistant/scripts/run_audit.py --employer-dir ~/Downloads/new-employer
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import datetime as dt
import hashlib
import json
import shutil
import sys
from pathlib import Path

SKILL_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
REPO = SKILL_DIR.parent.parent

from allocate import allocate  # noqa: E402
from employer import EmployerFileError, load_employer  # noqa: E402
from fetch_drive import FetchError, fetch_folder  # noqa: E402
from guide import GuideError, load_guide  # noqa: E402
from render import QUESTIONS_TITLE, REPORT_TITLE, codes_csv, merge_sections, questions_section, report_section, run_record  # noqa: E402


def sha256(path: Path) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Suggest class codes, allocate payroll and draft audit questions.")
    pick = ap.add_mutually_exclusive_group(required=True)
    pick.add_argument("--employer", action="append", metavar="SLUG", help="employer folder name, for example harbor-point-legal (repeatable)")
    pick.add_argument("--all", action="store_true", help="every employer folder in the source")
    pick.add_argument("--employer-dir", type=Path, help="a local employer folder that is not in the Drive folder")
    ap.add_argument("--source-dir", type=Path, help="use a local copy of the audit folder instead of reading Drive")
    ap.add_argument("--cache-dir", type=Path, default=REPO / ".cache" / "drive", help="where the Drive folder is downloaded")
    ap.add_argument("--out", type=Path, default=REPO, help="repository root to write deliverables/ and runs/ into")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)

    config = json.loads((SKILL_DIR / "sources.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    sources = {"guide_file": config["guide_file"], "employers_folder": config["employers_folder"]}
    try:
        if args.source_dir:
            root = args.source_dir.expanduser().resolve()
            sources["read_from"] = f"local copy {root}"
        else:
            root = args.cache_dir.resolve()
            if root.exists():
                shutil.rmtree(root)
            fetch_folder(config["drive_folder_id"], root)
            sources["read_from"] = f"Google Drive folder '{config['drive_folder_name']}' ({config['drive_folder_id']})"
        sources["read_at_utc"] = dt.datetime.now(dt.timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
        guide_path = root / config["guide_file"]
        if not guide_path.exists():
            raise GuideError(f"classification guide {config['guide_file']} not found in {root}")
        guide = load_guide(guide_path)
    except (FetchError, GuideError) as exc:
        print(f"error: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

    employers_root = root / config["employers_folder"]
    if args.employer_dir:
        folders = [args.employer_dir.expanduser().resolve()]
    else:
        available = sorted(p.name for p in employers_root.iterdir() if p.is_dir()) if employers_root.is_dir() else []
        wanted = available if args.all else args.employer
        missing = [s for s in wanted if s not in available]
        if missing:
            print(f"error: no employer folder named {', '.join(missing)}; available: {', '.join(available) or 'none'}", file=sys.stderr)
            return 1
        folders = [employers_root / s for s in wanted]

    out = args.out.resolve()
    (out / "deliverables" / "codes").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    (out / "runs").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    order = config.get("report_order", [])
    failed = 0
    for folder in folders:
        try:
            emp = load_employer(folder)
            result = allocate(emp, guide)
        except (EmployerFileError, GuideError, ValueError) as exc:
            failed += 1
            print(f"error: {folder.name}: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
            continue
        (out / "deliverables" / "codes" / f"{emp.slug}.csv").write_text(codes_csv(result), encoding="utf-8")
        merge_sections(out / "deliverables" / "audit-report.md", REPORT_TITLE, emp.slug, report_section(result), order)
        merge_sections(out / "deliverables" / "audit-questions.md", QUESTIONS_TITLE, emp.slug, questions_section(result), order)
        files = {p.name: sha256(p) for p in sorted(folder.iterdir()) if p.is_file()}
        record = run_record(result, {**sources, "guide_sha256": sha256(guide_path), "employer_files_sha256": files})
        (out / "runs" / f"{emp.slug}.json").write_text(json.dumps(record, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
        verdict = "accepted" if result.accepted else "not accepted"
        codes = ", ".join(f"{c} {a:.2f}" for c, a, _ in result.lines())
        print(f"{emp.slug}: employer split {verdict}; {codes}; {len(result.adjustments)} adjustments, {len(result.questions)} questions")
    return 1 if failed else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""Run the class-code assistant on one or more employer files.

Reads the classification guide and the employer files from the audit team's Drive
folder at the start of every run (or from a local copy given with --source-dir),
then writes, per employer:

    deliverables/codes/<employer>.csv
    deliverables/audit-report.md      (the employer's section)
    deliverables/audit-questions.md   (the employer's section)
    runs/<employer>.json              (run record: sources read, allocation, questions)

Examples:
    python3 skills/class-code-assistant/scripts/run_audit.py --employer harbor-point-legal
    python3 skills/class-code-assistant/scripts/run_audit.py --all
    python3 skills/class-code-assistant/scripts/run_audit.py --employer-dir ~/Downloads/new-employer
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import datetime as dt
import hashlib
import json
import shutil
import sys
from pathlib import Path

SKILL_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
REPO = SKILL_DIR.parent.parent

from allocate import allocate  # noqa: E402
from employer import EmployerFileError, load_employer  # noqa: E402
from fetch_drive import FetchError, fetch_folder  # noqa: E402
from guide import GuideError, load_guide  # noqa: E402
from render import QUESTIONS_TITLE, REPORT_TITLE, codes_csv, merge_sections, questions_section, report_section, run_record  # noqa: E402


def sha256(path: Path) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Suggest class codes, allocate payroll and draft audit questions.")
    pick = ap.add_mutually_exclusive_group(required=True)
    pick.add_argument("--employer", action="append", metavar="SLUG", help="employer folder name, for example harbor-point-legal (repeatable)")
    pick.add_argument("--all", action="store_true", help="every employer folder in the source")
    pick.add_argument("--employer-dir", type=Path, help="a local employer folder that is not in the Drive folder")
    ap.add_argument("--source-dir", type=Path, help="use a local copy of the audit folder instead of reading Drive")
    ap.add_argument("--cache-dir", type=Path, default=REPO / ".cache" / "drive", help="where the Drive folder is downloaded")
    ap.add_argument("--out", type=Path, default=REPO, help="repository root to write deliverables/ and runs/ into")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)

    config = json.loads((SKILL_DIR / "sources.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    sources = {"guide_file": config["guide_file"], "employers_folder": config["employers_folder"]}
    try:
        if args.source_dir:
            root = args.source_dir.expanduser().resolve()
            sources["read_from"] = f"local copy {root}"
        else:
            root = args.cache_dir.resolve()
            if root.exists():
                shutil.rmtree(root)
            fetch_folder(config["drive_folder_id"], root)
            sources["read_from"] = f"Google Drive folder '{config['drive_folder_name']}' ({config['drive_folder_id']})"
        sources["read_at_utc"] = dt.datetime.now(dt.timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
        guide_path = root / config["guide_file"]
        if not guide_path.exists():
            raise GuideError(f"classification guide {config['guide_file']} not found in {root}")
        guide = load_guide(guide_path)
    except (FetchError, GuideError) as exc:
        print(f"error: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

    employers_root = root / config["employers_folder"]
    if args.employer_dir:
        folders = [args.employer_dir.expanduser().resolve()]
    else:
        available = sorted(p.name for p in employers_root.iterdir() if p.is_dir()) if employers_root.is_dir() else []
        wanted = available if args.all else args.employer
        missing = [s for s in wanted if s not in available]
        if missing:
            print(f"error: no employer folder named {', '.join(missing)}; available: {', '.join(available) or 'none'}", file=sys.stderr)
            return 1
        folders = [employers_root / s for s in wanted]

    out = args.out.resolve()
    (out / "deliverables" / "codes").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    (out / "runs").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    order = config.get("report_order", [])
    failed = 0
    for folder in folders:
        try:
            emp = load_employer(folder)
            result = allocate(emp, guide)
        except (EmployerFileError, GuideError, ValueError) as exc:
            failed += 1
            print(f"error: {folder.name}: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
            continue
        (out / "deliverables" / "codes" / f"{emp.slug}.csv").write_text(codes_csv(result), encoding="utf-8")
        merge_sections(out / "deliverables" / "audit-report.md", REPORT_TITLE, emp.slug, report_section(result), order)
        merge_sections(out / "deliverables" / "audit-questions.md", QUESTIONS_TITLE, emp.slug, questions_section(result), order)
        files = {p.name: sha256(p) for p in sorted(folder.iterdir()) if p.is_file()}
        record = run_record(result, {**sources, "guide_sha256": sha256(guide_path), "employer_files_sha256": files})
        (out / "runs" / f"{emp.slug}.json").write_text(json.dumps(record, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
        verdict = "accepted" if result.accepted else "not accepted"
        codes = ", ".join(f"{c} {a:.2f}" for c, a, _ in result.lines())
        print(f"{emp.slug}: employer split {verdict}; {codes}; {len(result.adjustments)} adjustments, {len(result.questions)} questions")
    return 1 if failed else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

The Skill classifies and allocates payroll only; it does not set rates or quote premium. Each section says whether the
employer's own split is accepted, every adjustment with its amount, and the records that decided it. Paragraph
identifiers (CG-nn) are cited from the classification guide read during the run.

QUESTIONS_TITLE = """# Audit questions for the employers

subcontractor or record it is about. Every adjustment and every record the allocation relies on is covered by at least
one question.
"""


def codes_csv(result: Result) -> str:
    buf = io.StringIO()
    w = csv.writer(buf, lineterminator="\n")
    w.writerow(CSV_HEADER)
    for code, amount, ref in result.lines():
        w.writerow([code, f"{amount:.2f}", ref])
    return buf.getvalue()


def _md(text: str) -> str:
    return text.replace("|", "\\|")


def _decision(r: Result) -> str:
    reg = r.employer.record_files["payroll_register"]
    if r.accepted:
        others = [f for f in r.records_used if f not in (reg, "field-notes.md")]
        checked = f", checked against {', '.join(others)}" if others else ""
        return (f"**Decision: the employer's own split is accepted.** The payroll register ({reg}) gives the same codes and "
                f"amounts to the cent{checked}, and no record shows payroll that can be measured under another code.")
    files = []
    for a in r.adjustments:
        for f in a.records:
            if f not in files:
                files.append(f)
    return (f"**Decision: the employer's own split is not accepted.** The employer's records disagree with the application, "
            f"and the records decide. The allocation rests on {', '.join(files)}.")

    e = r.employer
    out = [f"## {e.name}", ""]
    files = ["application.md", "business-description.md"]

        files.append("field-notes.md")
    files += [f for f in e.record_files.values()]
    out.append(f"Application {e.application_id}. Audit period {e.period_start} to {e.period_end}. Classification guide "
               f"edition {r.guide.edition}. Employer file read: {', '.join(files)}.")
    if e.unused_files:
        out.append("Not used for the allocation: " + "; ".join(f"{k} ({v})" for k, v in e.unused_files.items()) + ".")
    out += ["", _decision(r), "", "### Codes and payroll allocated", "",
            "| Class code | Payroll allocated | Rationale ref | Code described as |", "|---|---:|---|---|"]

            "| Class code | Employer reported | Allocated | Difference |", "|---|---:|---:|---:|"]
    reported, alloc = r.reported, r.by_code

    for code in [c for c in r.guide.codes if c in reported or c in alloc]:
        rv, av = reported.get(code, ZERO), alloc.get(code, ZERO)

    out += [f"| Total | {rep_total:.2f} | {total:.2f} | {total - rep_total:+.2f} |", ""]
    if e.employer_note:
        out += [f"Employer's note on the application: \"{e.employer_note}\"", ""]
    if r.employer_assignment:
        names = {s.key: s.label for s in r.subjects}

            if diff:

                outs = [a for a in r.adjustments if a.from_code == code]
                parts = []
                if ins:
                    parts.append("in: " + "; ".join(f"{a.subject} {a.amount:.2f}" for a in ins))
                if outs:
                    parts.append("out: " + "; ".join(f"{a.subject} {a.amount:.2f}" for a in outs))
                out.append(f"- {code} {diff:+.2f} ({' | '.join(parts)})")
        out.append("")

    out += ["### Adjustments", ""]
    if r.adjustments:
        out += ["| # | Employee or payment | Amount | From | To | Why | Records | Guide |", "|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|---|"]
        for i, a in enumerate(r.adjustments, 1):

    else:
        out.append("None. Every employee's payroll stays under the code the employer reported.")
    out.append("")
    if r.excluded:
        out += ["### Paid but not counted as payroll", "", "| Employee or payment | Amount | Why |", "|---|---:|---|"]
        for who, amount, why in r.excluded:
            out.append(f"| {_md(who)} | {amount:.2f} | {_md(why)} |")
        out.append("")

    out += ["### Allocation by employee and payment", "", "| Employee or payment | Class code | Amount | Basis | Records |", "|---|---|---:|---|---|"]
    for s in r.subjects:

            out.append(f"| {_md(s.label)} | {p.code} | {p.amount:.2f} | {_md(p.basis)} | {', '.join(p.records)} |")

    for f, what in r.records_used.items():
        out.append(f"- {f}: {what}.")
    out.append("")
    if r.assumptions:
        out += ["### Assumptions where the guide is silent", ""]
        out += [f"- {a}" for a in r.assumptions]
        out.append("")
    if r.notes:
        out += ["### Notes", ""]
        out += [f"- {n}" for n in r.notes]
        out.append("")
    return "\n".join(out).rstrip() + "\n"


def questions_section(r: Result) -> str:
    out = [f"## {r.employer.name}", ""]
    for i, q in enumerate(r.questions, 1):
        out.append(f"{i}. **{q.subject}.** {q.text}")
    return "\n".join(out) + "\n"


SECTION_RE = re.compile(r"<!-- BEGIN employer:(?P<slug>[a-z0-9-]+) -->\n(?P<body>.*?)<!-- END employer:(?P=slug) -->\n", re.S)


def merge_sections(path: Path, title: str, slug: str, body: str, order: list[str]) -> None:
    """Insert or replace one employer's section; keep sections in the configured order."""
    sections: dict[str, str] = {}
    if path.exists():

    parts = [title]
    for s in ranked:
        parts.append(f"<!-- BEGIN employer:{s} -->\n{sections[s]}<!-- END employer:{s} -->\n")
    path.write_text("\n".join(parts), encoding="utf-8")


def run_record(r: Result, sources: dict) -> dict:
    def d(x: Decimal) -> str:
        return f"{x:.2f}"

    return {
        "employer": r.employer.slug,
        "name": r.employer.name,
        "application": r.employer.application_id,
        "audit_period": [str(r.employer.period_start), str(r.employer.period_end)],

            for s in r.subjects

        "adjustments": [{"subject": a.subject, "amount": d(a.amount), "from": a.from_code, "to": a.to_code, "reason": a.reason, "records": a.records, "refs": a.refs} for a in r.adjustments],

from pathlib import Path

employer's own split is accepted, every adjustment with its amount, and the records that decided it. Paragraph
identifiers (CG-nn) are cited from the classification guide read during the run.

QUESTIONS_TITLE = """# Audit questions for the employers

Questions for the premium auditor to put to each employer before signing off. Each one names the employee,
subcontractor or record it is about. Every adjustment and every record the allocation relies on is covered by at least
one question.
"""


def codes_csv(result: Result) -> str:
    buf = io.StringIO()
    w = csv.writer(buf, lineterminator="\n")
    w.writerow(CSV_HEADER)
    for code, amount, ref in result.lines():
        w.writerow([code, f"{amount:.2f}", ref])
    return buf.getvalue()


def _md(text: str) -> str:
    return text.replace("|", "\\|")


def _decision(r: Result) -> str:
    reg = r.employer.record_files["payroll_register"]
    if r.accepted:
        others = [f for f in r.records_used if f not in (reg, "field-notes.md")]
        checked = f", checked against {', '.join(others)}" if others else ""
        open_points = [n for n in r.notes if n.startswith("Field notes:")]
        tail = (" The field notes describe some work under another code, but with no time records to measure it the split "
                "does not change; the employer is asked for those records (see Notes and the audit questions).") if open_points else ""
        return (f"**Decision: the employer's own split is accepted.** The payroll register ({reg}) gives the same codes and "
                f"amounts to the cent{checked}, and no record shows payroll that can be measured under another code.{tail}")
    files = []
    for a in r.adjustments:
        for f in a.records:
            if f not in files:
                files.append(f)
    return (f"**Decision: the employer's own split is not accepted.** The employer's records disagree with the application, "
            f"and the records decide. The allocation rests on {', '.join(files)}.")


def report_section(r: Result) -> str:
    e = r.employer
    out = [f"## {e.name}", ""]
    files = ["application.md", "business-description.md"]

    out.append(f"Application {e.application_id}. Audit period {e.period_start} to {e.period_end}. Classification guide "
               f"edition {r.guide.edition}. Employer file read: {', '.join(files)}.")

    total = ZERO

        total += amount
    out += [f"| Total | {total:.2f} | | |", "", f"Principal business code: {r.governing_code}; {r.governing_basis}.", ""]

    out += ["### Compared with the employer's own split", "",
            "| Class code | Employer reported | Allocated | Difference |", "|---|---:|---:|---:|"]
    reported, alloc = r.reported, r.by_code

        rv, av = reported.get(code, ZERO), alloc.get(code, ZERO)
        rep_total += rv
        out.append(f"| {code} | {rv:.2f} | {av:.2f} | {av - rv:+.2f} |")
    out += [f"| Total | {rep_total:.2f} | {total:.2f} | {total - rep_total:+.2f} |", ""]
    if e.employer_note:
        out += [f"Employer's note on the application: \"{e.employer_note}\"", ""]
    if r.employer_assignment:
        names = {s.key: s.label for s in r.subjects}
        per_code: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
        for eid, code in r.employer_assignment.items():
            per_code.setdefault(code, []).append(names[eid])
        out.append("The employer's figures match these employees on the register: "
                   + "; ".join(f"{c}: {', '.join(n)}" for c, n in per_code.items()) + ".")
        out.append("")
    if not r.accepted:
        out.append("Where and why the allocation differs:")
        out.append("")
        for code in [c for c in r.guide.codes if c in reported or c in alloc]:
            diff = alloc.get(code, ZERO) - reported.get(code, ZERO)
            if diff:
                ins = [a for a in r.adjustments if a.to_code == code]
                outs = [a for a in r.adjustments if a.from_code == code]
                parts = []
                if ins:
                    parts.append("in: " + "; ".join(f"{a.subject} {a.amount:.2f}" for a in ins))
                if outs:
                    parts.append("out: " + "; ".join(f"{a.subject} {a.amount:.2f}" for a in outs))
                out.append(f"- {code} {diff:+.2f} ({' | '.join(parts)})")
        out.append("")

    out += ["### Adjustments", ""]
    if r.adjustments:
        out += ["| # | Employee or payment | Amount | From | To | Why | Records | Guide |", "|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|---|"]
        for i, a in enumerate(r.adjustments, 1):
            out.append(f"| {i} | {_md(a.subject)} | {a.amount:.2f} | {a.from_code or 'not reported'} | {a.to_code or 'not counted'} | "
                       f"{_md(a.reason)} | {', '.join(a.records)} | {', '.join(a.refs)} |")
    else:
        out.append("None. Every employee's payroll stays under the code the employer reported.")
    out.append("")
    if r.excluded:
        out += ["### Paid but not counted as payroll", "", "| Employee or payment | Amount | Why |", "|---|---:|---|"]
        for who, amount, why in r.excluded:
            out.append(f"| {_md(who)} | {amount:.2f} | {_md(why)} |")
        out.append("")

    out += ["### Allocation by employee and payment", "", "| Employee or payment | Class code | Amount | Basis | Records |", "|---|---|---:|---|---|"]
    for s in r.subjects:
        for p in s.portions:
            out.append(f"| {_md(s.label)} | {p.code} | {p.amount:.2f} | {_md(p.basis)} | {', '.join(p.records)} |")
    out += ["", "### Records that decided this file", ""]
    for f, what in r.records_used.items():
        out.append(f"- {f}: {what}.")
    out.append("")
    if r.assumptions:
        out += ["### Assumptions where the guide is silent", ""]
        out += [f"- {a}" for a in r.assumptions]
        out.append("")
    if r.notes:
        out += ["### Notes", ""]
        out += [f"- {n}" for n in r.notes]
        out.append("")
    return "\n".join(out).rstrip() + "\n"


def questions_section(r: Result) -> str:
    out = [f"## {r.employer.name}", ""]
    for i, q in enumerate(r.questions, 1):
        out.append(f"{i}. **{q.subject.rstrip('.')}.** {q.text}")
    return "\n".join(out) + "\n"


SECTION_RE = re.compile(r"<!-- BEGIN employer:(?P<slug>[a-z0-9-]+) -->\n(?P<body>.*?)<!-- END employer:(?P=slug) -->\n", re.S)


def merge_sections(path: Path, title: str, slug: str, body: str, order: list[str]) -> None:
    """Insert or replace one employer's section; keep sections in the configured order."""
    sections: dict[str, str] = {}
    if path.exists():
        for m in SECTION_RE.finditer(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")):
            sections[m.group("slug")] = m.group("body")
    sections[slug] = body
    ranked = sorted(sections, key=lambda s: (order.index(s) if s in order else len(order), s))
    parts = [title]
    for s in ranked:
        parts.append(f"<!-- BEGIN employer:{s} -->\n{sections[s]}<!-- END employer:{s} -->\n")
    path.write_text("\n".join(parts), encoding="utf-8")

    def d(x: Decimal) -> str:
        return f"{x:.2f}"

    return {
        "employer": r.employer.slug,
        "name": r.employer.name,

            out.append(f"| {_md(who)} | {amount:.2f} | {_md(why)} |")
        out.append("")

    out += ["### Allocation by employee and payment", "", "| Employee or payment | Class code | Amount | Basis | Records |", "|---|---|---:|---|---|"]
    for s in r.subjects:
        for p in s.portions:
            out.append(f"| {_md(s.label)} | {p.code} | {p.amount:.2f} | {_md(p.basis)} | {', '.join(p.records)} |")
    out += ["", "### Records that decided this file", ""]
    for f, what in r.records_used.items():
        out.append(f"- {f}: {what}.")
    out.append("")
    if r.assumptions:
        out += ["### Assumptions where the guide is silent", ""]
        out += [f"- {a}" for a in r.assumptions]
        out.append("")
    if r.notes:
        out += ["### Notes", ""]
        out += [f"- {n}" for n in r.notes]
        out.append("")
    return "\n".join(out).rstrip() + "\n"


def questions_section(r: Result) -> str:
    out = [f"## {r.employer.name}", ""]
    for i, q in enumerate(r.questions, 1):
        out.append(f"{i}. **{q.subject.rstrip('.')}.** {q.text}")
    return "\n".join(out) + "\n"


SECTION_RE = re.compile(r"<!-- BEGIN employer:(?P<slug>[a-z0-9-]+) -->\n(?P<body>.*?)<!-- END employer:(?P=slug) -->\n", re.S)


def merge_sections(path: Path, title: str, slug: str, body: str, order: list[str]) -> None:
    """Insert or replace one employer's section; keep sections in the configured order."""
    sections: dict[str, str] = {}
    if path.exists():
        for m in SECTION_RE.finditer(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")):
            sections[m.group("slug")] = m.group("body")
    sections[slug] = body
    ranked = sorted(sections, key=lambda s: (order.index(s) if s in order else len(order), s))
    parts = [title]
    for s in ranked:
        parts.append(f"<!-- BEGIN employer:{s} -->\n{sections[s]}<!-- END employer:{s} -->\n")
    path.write_text("\n".join(parts), encoding="utf-8")


def run_record(r: Result, sources: dict) -> dict:
    def d(x: Decimal) -> str:
        return f"{x:.2f}"

    return {

             "portions": [{"code": p.code, "amount": d(p.amount), "basis": p.basis, "records": p.records, "refs": p.refs} for p in s.portions]}
            for s in r.subjects
        ],
        "excluded": [{"label": w, "amount": d(a), "why": y} for w, a, y in r.excluded],
        "adjustments": [{"subject": a.subject, "amount": d(a.amount), "from": a.from_code, "to": a.to_code, "reason": a.reason, "records": a.records, "refs": a.refs} for a in r.adjustments],

    }

"""Check the Skill's outputs against the assignment's format rules and the source records.

Run after run_audit.py. It re-reads the guide and the payroll registers from the same
source the run used (the Drive cache by default) and checks, for every employer:

- deliverables/codes/<employer>.csv exists, has exactly the header
  class_code,payroll_allocated,rationale_ref, one row per code, no zero rows,
  dollars to the cent without separators, and a rationale_ref that is the guide
  paragraph describing that code;
- the CSV total equals the payroll register total plus the additions the run reports
  (uninsured subcontractors, undocumented allowances), and every employee's portions
  add up to the register wages;
- audit-report.md and audit-questions.md have one section per employer; the report
  shows every code, amount and adjustment; every adjustment and every record relied on
  is named in at least one question, and every question names its subject.

Exit status 0 when every check passes, 1 otherwise.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import json
import re
import sys
from decimal import Decimal
from pathlib import Path

SKILL_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
REPO = SKILL_DIR.parent.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))

from guide import load_guide  # noqa: E402
from render import SECTION_RE  # noqa: E402

AMOUNT_RE = re.compile(r"^\d+\.\d{2}$")


def sections(path: Path) -> dict[str, str]:
    return {m.group("slug"): m.group("body") for m in SECTION_RE.finditer(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))}


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    ap.add_argument("--source-dir", type=Path, default=REPO / ".cache" / "drive")
    ap.add_argument("--out", type=Path, default=REPO)
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    config = json.loads((SKILL_DIR / "sources.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    src, out = args.source_dir.resolve(), args.out.resolve()
    guide = load_guide(src / config["guide_file"])
    failures: list[str] = []
    checks = 0

    def check(ok: bool, message: str) -> None:
        nonlocal checks
        checks += 1
        if not ok:
            failures.append(message)

    runs = sorted((out / "runs").glob("*.json"))
    check(bool(runs), "no run records in runs/; run run_audit.py first")
    slugs = [r.stem for r in runs]
    for expected in config.get("report_order", []):
        check(expected in slugs, f"no run for {expected}")
    report = sections(out / "deliverables" / "audit-report.md")
    questions = sections(out / "deliverables" / "audit-questions.md")

    for run_path in runs:
        run = json.loads(run_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        slug = run["employer"]
        where = slug

        # CSV format.
        csv_path = out / "deliverables" / "codes" / f"{slug}.csv"
        check(csv_path.exists(), f"{where}: {csv_path.name} missing")
        if not csv_path.exists():
            continue
        raw = csv_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        check(raw.splitlines()[0] == "class_code,payroll_allocated,rationale_ref", f"{where}: CSV header is not exact")
        rows = list(csv.DictReader(raw.splitlines()))
        codes_seen = set()
        csv_total = Decimal("0")
        for row in rows:
            code, amount, ref = row["class_code"], row["payroll_allocated"], row["rationale_ref"]
            check(code not in codes_seen, f"{where}: {code} appears twice")
            codes_seen.add(code)
            check(guide.has_code(code), f"{where}: {code} is not in the guide")
            check(bool(AMOUNT_RE.match(amount)), f"{where}: {code} amount {amount!r} is not dollars to the cent without separators")
            check(Decimal(amount) > 0, f"{where}: {code} has zero payroll")
            if guide.has_code(code):
                check(ref == guide.code_paragraph(code).id, f"{where}: {code} cites {ref}, the guide describes it in {guide.code_paragraph(code).id}")
            check(ref in guide.paragraphs, f"{where}: rationale_ref {ref} is not a paragraph of the guide")
            csv_total += Decimal(amount)

        # Totals against the payroll register read again from the source.
        reg_name = next((f for f, what in run["records_used"].items() if what.startswith("gross wages")), "payroll-register.csv")
        reg_rows = list(csv.DictReader((src / config["employers_folder"] / slug / reg_name).open(encoding="utf-8")))
        reg_total = sum(Decimal(r["wages_paid"]) for r in reg_rows)
        additions = sum(Decimal(a["amount"]) for a in run["adjustments"] if a["from"] is None and a["to"])
        removed = sum(Decimal(a["amount"]) for a in run["adjustments"] if a["to"] is None)
        owners_out = sum(Decimal(e["amount"]) for e in run["excluded"] if "election of exclusion" in e["why"])
        check(csv_total == reg_total + additions - removed - owners_out,
              f"{where}: CSV total {csv_total} != register {reg_total} + additions {additions} - removed {removed + owners_out}")
        wages = {f"{r['name']} ({r['employee_id']})": Decimal(r["wages_paid"]) for r in reg_rows}
        for s in run["subjects"]:
            if s["kind"] != "employee":
                continue
            base = sum(Decimal(p["amount"]) for p in s["portions"] if "allowance not backed" not in p["basis"])
            check(base == wages.get(s["label"]), f"{where}: {s['label']} portions {base} != register wages {wages.get(s['label'])}")
        check(len([s for s in run["subjects"] if s["kind"] == "employee"]) + sum(1 for e in run["excluded"] if "election of exclusion" in e["why"]) == len(reg_rows),
              f"{where}: not every employee on the register was allocated")

        # Report section.
        body = report.get(slug, "")
        check(bool(body), f"{where}: no section in audit-report.md")
        check(f"## {run['name']}" in body, f"{where}: report section heading is not the employer name")
        for row in rows:
            check(f"| {row['class_code']} | {row['payroll_allocated']} | {row['rationale_ref']} |" in body, f"{where}: report does not show {row['class_code']} {row['payroll_allocated']}")
        decision = "accepted.**" if run["accepted_employer_split"] else "not accepted.**"
        check(decision in body, f"{where}: report decision does not match the run")
        for a in run["adjustments"]:

# Decision rules

How the Skill turns an employer file into codes and payroll. Paragraph identifiers are those of the July 2025
classification guide excerpt; the scripts find the general paragraphs by title at run time, so a renumbered guide still
works, and every code citation in the outputs is read from the guide fetched during the run.

## Rules taken from the guide

| Rule | Guide | What the Skill does |
|---|---|---|
| Records decide | (assignment) | The employer's application is compared, never copied. Where records and the application disagree, the records decide. |
| Payroll | CG-03 | Payroll is `wages_paid` on the payroll register. An allowance paid on top of wages is left out only when it is a documented expense (see assumption A3). |
| Owners | CG-05 | An owner or officer with an election of exclusion who is not on the register is not counted. An owner on the register without an election is counted under the code for the owner's own work. |
| Assigning codes | CG-02 | Each employee starts under the code that describes the job on the register (`position-map.csv`). |
| Clerical | CG-04 | The office code applies only to duties confined to an office. |
| Division | CG-07 | Payroll is divided between codes only when the employer keeps records of time in each: crew timesheets with a type of work (divided by hours), or a route log that shows office staff on delivery vehicles (divided by days, priced with the weekly payroll). |
| Subcontractors | CG-06 | A payment to a subcontractor without a workers' compensation certificate covering the payment date is payroll under the code for the subcontractor's work. |
| Citation | Code paragraphs | `rationale_ref` is the identifier of the paragraph that describes the code. |

## House assumptions where the guide is silent

The interview with the auditor was not conducted in this test, so these are stated assumptions. Each one produces a
question to the employer, and each is printed in the report section of every employer it affects.

- **A1. Office staff at job sites.** An office-coded employee who signs in at a job site is not confined to an office
  (CG-04). Without time records (CG-07) the whole payroll goes to the principal business code (CG-02), however few the
  visits. If the business has no code other than the office code, the employee stays there and the visits are asked
  about.
- **A2. Principal business.** The principal business (CG-02) is the code with the most payroll outside the office code,
  measured from the records after timesheet and route-log division. With no such payroll, it is the employer's largest
  reported code.
- **A3. Allowances.** For an allowance column with a matching days column (for example `travel_allowance_paid` and
  `travel_days`), the part backed by recorded days at the most common per-day amount is a documented expense (CG-03).
  Anything paid beyond that, or with no recorded days, is payroll under the employee's code. A per-day amount that
  differs from the common one is asked about.
- **A4. Route-log division.** A day on a delivery vehicle counts as a full day of that code's work. The days an employee
  works in a week are taken as the operating days in the route log for that week, since office staff have no
  attendance record. The question to the employer says the share rises if the employee works fewer days.
- **A5. Subcontractor names.** A payment name that is a shortened form of a certificate holder's name (for example
  without "LLC" or a second trade) is taken as the same company, and the employer is asked to confirm it.
- **A6. Subcontractor amounts and dates.** The full amount paid to an uninsured subcontractor is payroll, and the
  payment date stands for the date of the work, because the files have no labor and material split and no work dates.
- **A7. Mixed duties without time records.** Payroll is never divided on a narrative, a job title or sales figures
  (for example receipts split between dining room and catering). The employee stays under the code of the job on the
  register, and the employer is asked for time records.

## Narrative check

Field notes are read sentence by sentence. A sentence that names a position on the register together with a word from
the title of another code the employer reports (for example "restaurant" for F-710 next to "catering lead") is reported
as an open point with a question. It never changes the allocation by itself (A7).

## Out of scope

Rates and premium (CG-01 describes the premium basis only so the payroll basis is clear). The Skill does not set rates,
apply experience modifiers or quote premium.

---
name: class-code-assistant
description: First-pass premium audit for a Linden Shore Mutual workers' compensation employer file. Reads the company's classification guide and the employer's records from the audit team's Drive folder, suggests class codes, allocates payroll to them, compares the result with the employer's own split, and drafts the questions the auditor should put to the employer. Use when an auditor asks to classify, allocate payroll for, or prepare audit questions on an employer file. It does not set rates or quote premium.
---

# Class code assistant

Does the first pass on an employer file for the premium audit team: suggest the class codes, allocate the payroll to
them, and list the questions to put to the employer before sign-off. The company uses its own class codes, so only the
classification guide in the audit folder is used; public classification manuals do not apply.

## Inputs

- **Classification guide**: `classification-guide.md` in the audit team's Drive folder "CH03 premium audit"
  (folder id in `sources.json`). Read fresh on every run.
- **Employer file**: one folder per employer under `employer-files/` in the same Drive folder, named with the employer
  slug (for example `harbor-point-legal`). Required: `application.md` (the employer's own split),
  `business-description.md` (audit period, owners), `payroll-register.csv`
  (`employee_id,name,position,wages_paid`, optionally `<x>_days,<x>_allowance_paid`). Used when present, recognised by
  their columns: crew timesheets (`date,employee_id,work_type,hours`), site sign-in log (`date,employee_id,site`), route
  log (`date,route_id,driver_id,ride_along_id`), weekly payroll (`week_start,week_end,employee_id,gross_pay`),
  subcontractor payments (`date,subcontractor,work,amount_paid`), insurance certificates
  (`subcontractor,coverage_from,coverage_to`), and `field-notes.md`. Any other file is listed in the report as not used.
- A local copy of the folder can be used instead of Drive with `--source-dir`, and a single employer folder outside
  Drive with `--employer-dir`.

## Invocation

From the repository root (Python 3.9 or later, standard library only):

```sh
python3 skills/class-code-assistant/scripts/run_audit.py --employer harbor-point-legal   # one employer
python3 skills/class-code-assistant/scripts/run_audit.py --all                          # every employer in the folder
python3 skills/class-code-assistant/scripts/verify_outputs.py                           # check the outputs
```

When an agent runs this Skill:

1. Run `run_audit.py` for the employer(s) asked for. It downloads the Drive folder into `.cache/drive/` first.
2. Read the employer's `field-notes.md`, `business-description.md` and the application note, then read the employer's
   section of `deliverables/audit-report.md`. Check that every statement in the narrative is either reflected in an
   adjustment, an assumption, a note or a question. If something is missing, say so to the auditor; do not edit the
   generated files by hand.
3. Run `verify_outputs.py` and report its result.
4. Tell the auditor, per employer, whether the employer's own split is accepted and which record that rests on.

## Outputs

Paths are relative to the repository root (`--out` changes the root).

| Path | Content |
|---|---|
| `deliverables/codes/<employer>.csv` | `class_code,payroll_allocated,rationale_ref`; one row per code with payroll, dollars to the cent, no separators; `rationale_ref` is the guide paragraph describing the code. |
| `deliverables/audit-report.md` | One section per employer: decision on the employer's split, codes and payroll, comparison with the employer's split, every adjustment with its amount, records relied on, assumptions, notes. |
| `deliverables/audit-questions.md` | One section per employer: questions that each name an employee, subcontractor or record. |
| `runs/<employer>.json` | Run record: where the sources were read from, SHA-256 of every file read, the allocation per employee and payment, adjustments and questions. |

A run on one employer replaces only that employer's sections in the two Markdown files.

## Error behavior

- Drive folder not reachable or not shared publicly: prints `error: ...` and exits 1 without writing anything.
- Guide missing, or missing a general paragraph the rules need (Assigning codes, Payroll, Owners and executive
  officers, Subcontractors, Division of payroll), or a vocabulary map that uses a code the guide does not describe:
  exits 1 without writing anything.
- Employer folder missing a required file, a malformed amount or date, or a duplicated employee: that employer is
  skipped with `error: <employer>: ...`, the others are still processed, and the exit status is 1.
- A position, type of work or subcontractor trade that matches no code is not guessed: the employee or payment goes
  under the principal business code and a question asks the employer to describe the work.

## Supporting files

- `scripts/fetch_drive.py`: downloads the public Drive folder (falls back to the system `curl` when Python has no CA
  certificates).
- `scripts/guide.py`: parses the guide into paragraphs and codes.
- `scripts/employer.py`: loads an employer folder; recognises records by their columns.
- `scripts/allocate.py`: the classification and allocation rules.
- `scripts/render.py`: writes the CSV, report and question sections and the run record.
- `scripts/run_audit.py`: command line entry point.
- `scripts/verify_outputs.py`: checks the outputs against the format rules and the source records.
- `references/decision-rules.md`: the rules, the guide paragraphs they rest on, and the house assumptions where the

# Decision rules

How the Skill turns an employer file into codes and payroll. Paragraph identifiers are those of the July 2025
classification guide excerpt; the scripts find the general paragraphs by title at run time, so a renumbered guide still
works, and every code citation in the outputs is read from the guide fetched during the run.

## Rules taken from the guide

| Rule | Guide | What the Skill does |
|---|---|---|
| Records decide | (assignment) | The employer's application is compared, never copied. Where records and the application disagree, the records decide. |
| Payroll | CG-03 | Payroll is `wages_paid` on the payroll register. An allowance paid on top of wages is left out only when it is a documented expense (see assumption A3). |
| Owners | CG-05 | An owner or officer with an election of exclusion who is not on the register is not counted. An owner on the register without an election is counted under the code for the owner's own work. |
| Assigning codes | CG-02 | Each employee starts under the code that describes the job on the register (`position-map.csv`). |
| Clerical | CG-04 | The office code applies only to duties confined to an office. |
| Division | CG-07 | Payroll is divided between codes only when the employer keeps records of time in each: crew timesheets with a type of work (divided by hours), or a route log that shows office staff on delivery vehicles (divided by days, priced with the weekly payroll). |
| Subcontractors | CG-06 | A payment to a subcontractor without a workers' compensation certificate covering the payment date is payroll under the code for the subcontractor's work. |
| Citation | Code paragraphs | `rationale_ref` is the identifier of the paragraph that describes the code. |

## House assumptions where the guide is silent

The interview with the auditor was not conducted in this test, so these are stated assumptions. Each one produces a
question to the employer, and each is printed in the report section of every employer it affects.

- **A1. Office staff at job sites.** An office-coded employee who signs in at a job site is not confined to an office
  (CG-04). Without time records (CG-07) the whole payroll goes to the principal business code (CG-02), however few the
  visits. If the business has no code other than the office code, the employee stays there and the visits are asked
  about.
- **A2. Principal business.** The principal business (CG-02) is the code with the most payroll outside the office code,
  measured from the records after timesheet and route-log division. With no such payroll, it is the employer's largest
  reported code.
- **A3. Allowances.** For an allowance column with a matching days column (for example `travel_allowance_paid` and
  `travel_days`), the part backed by recorded days at the most common per-day amount is a documented expense (CG-03).
  Anything paid beyond that, or with no recorded days, is payroll under the employee's code. A per-day amount that
  differs from the common one is asked about.
- **A4. Route-log division.** A day on a delivery vehicle counts as a full day of that code's work. The days an employee
  works in a week are taken as the operating days in the route log for that week, since office staff have no
  attendance record. The question to the employer says the share rises if the employee works fewer days.
- **A5. Subcontractor names.** A payment name that is a shortened form of a certificate holder's name (for example
  without "LLC" or a second trade) is taken as the same company, and the employer is asked to confirm it.
- **A6. Subcontractor amounts and dates.** The full amount paid to an uninsured subcontractor is payroll, and the
  payment date stands for the date of the work, because the files have no labor and material split and no work dates.
- **A7. Mixed duties without time records.** Payroll is never divided on a narrative, a job title or sales figures
  (for example receipts split between dining room and catering). The employee stays under the code of the job on the
  register, and the employer is asked for time records.

## Narrative check

Field notes are read sentence by sentence. A sentence that names a position on the register together with a word from
the title of another code the employer reports (for example "restaurant" for F-710 next to "catering lead") is reported
as an open point with a question. It never changes the allocation by itself (A7).

## Out of scope

Rates and premium (CG-01 describes the premium basis only so the payroll basis is clear). The Skill does not set rates,
apply experience modifiers or quote premium.

---
name: class-code-assistant
description: First-pass premium audit for a Linden Shore Mutual workers' compensation employer file. Reads the company's classification guide and the employer's records from the audit team's Drive folder, suggests class codes, allocates payroll to them, compares the result with the employer's own split, and drafts the questions the auditor should put to the employer. Use when an auditor asks to classify, allocate payroll for, or prepare audit questions on an employer file. It does not set rates or quote premium.
---

# Class code assistant

Does the first pass on an employer file for the premium audit team: suggest the class codes, allocate the payroll to
them, and list the questions to put to the employer before sign-off. The company uses its own class codes, so only the
classification guide in the audit folder is used; public classification manuals do not apply.

## Inputs

- **Classification guide**: `classification-guide.md` in the audit team's Drive folder "CH03 premium audit"
  (folder id in `sources.json`). Read fresh on every run.
- **Employer file**: one folder per employer under `employer-files/` in the same Drive folder, named with the employer
  slug (for example `harbor-point-legal`). Required: `application.md` (the employer's own split),
  `business-description.md` (audit period, owners), `payroll-register.csv`
  (`employee_id,name,position,wages_paid`, optionally `<x>_days,<x>_allowance_paid`). Used when present, recognised by
  their columns: crew timesheets (`date,employee_id,work_type,hours`), site sign-in log (`date,employee_id,site`), route
  log (`date,route_id,driver_id,ride_along_id`), weekly payroll (`week_start,week_end,employee_id,gross_pay`),
  subcontractor payments (`date,subcontractor,work,amount_paid`), insurance certificates
  (`subcontractor,coverage_from,coverage_to`), and `field-notes.md`. Any other file is listed in the report as not used.
- A local copy of the folder can be used instead of Drive with `--source-dir`, and a single employer folder outside
  Drive with `--employer-dir`.

## Invocation

From the repository root (Python 3.9 or later, standard library only):

```sh
python3 skills/class-code-assistant/scripts/run_audit.py --employer harbor-point-legal   # one employer
python3 skills/class-code-assistant/scripts/run_audit.py --all                          # every employer in the folder
python3 skills/class-code-assistant/scripts/verify_outputs.py                           # check the outputs
```

When an agent runs this Skill:

1. Run `run_audit.py` for the employer(s) asked for. It downloads the Drive folder into `.cache/drive/` first.
2. Read the employer's `field-notes.md`, `business-description.md` and the application note, then read the employer's
   section of `deliverables/audit-report.md`. Check that every statement in the narrative is either reflected in an
   adjustment, an assumption, a note or a question. If something is missing, say so to the auditor; do not edit the
   generated files by hand.
3. Run `verify_outputs.py` and report its result.
4. Tell the auditor, per employer, whether the employer's own split is accepted and which record that rests on.

## Outputs

Paths are relative to the repository root (`--out` changes the root).

| Path | Content |
|---|---|
| `deliverables/codes/<employer>.csv` | `class_code,payroll_allocated,rationale_ref`; one row per code with payroll, dollars to the cent, no separators; `rationale_ref` is the guide paragraph describing the code. |
| `deliverables/audit-report.md` | One section per employer: decision on the employer's split, codes and payroll, comparison with the employer's split, every adjustment with its amount, records relied on, assumptions, notes. |
| `deliverables/audit-questions.md` | One section per employer: questions that each name an employee, subcontractor or record. |
| `runs/<employer>.json` | Run record: where the sources were read from, SHA-256 of every file read, the allocation per employee and payment, adjustments and questions. |

A run on one employer replaces only that employer's sections in the two Markdown files.

## Error behavior

- Drive folder not reachable or not shared publicly: prints `error: ...` and exits 1 without writing anything.
- Guide missing, or missing a general paragraph the rules need (Assigning codes, Payroll, Owners and executive
  officers, Subcontractors, Division of payroll), or a vocabulary map that uses a code the guide does not describe:
  exits 1 without writing anything.
- Employer folder missing a required file, a malformed amount or date, or a duplicated employee: that employer is
  skipped with `error: <employer>: ...`, the others are still processed, and the exit status is 1.
- A position, type of work or subcontractor trade that matches no code is not guessed: the employee or payment goes
  under the principal business code and a question asks the employer to describe the work.

## Supporting files

- `scripts/fetch_drive.py`: downloads the public Drive folder (falls back to the system `curl` when Python has no CA
  certificates).
- `scripts/guide.py`: parses the guide into paragraphs and codes.
- `scripts/employer.py`: loads an employer folder; recognises records by their columns.
- `scripts/allocate.py`: the classification and allocation rules.
- `scripts/render.py`: writes the CSV, report and question sections and the run record.
- `scripts/run_audit.py`: command line entry point.
- `scripts/verify_outputs.py`: checks the outputs against the format rules and the source records.
- `references/decision-rules.md`: the rules, the guide paragraphs they rest on, and the house assumptions where the
  guide is silent.
- `references/position-map.csv`, `references/work-type-map.csv`: job titles and types of work matched to class codes;
  every code in them must exist in the guide or the run stops.
- `sources.json`: the Drive folder, file names, and the order of sections in the combined reports.

# Class Code and Premium Audit Assistant

A reusable Agent Skill that does the premium audit team's first pass on a Linden Shore Mutual workers' compensation
employer file: it suggests the class codes, allocates the payroll to them, compares the result with the employer's own
split, and drafts the questions the auditor should put to the employer. It classifies and allocates payroll only; it
does not set rates or quote premium.

The Skill lives in [`skills/class-code-assistant/`](skills/class-code-assistant/SKILL.md). Its rules and the
assumptions made where the classification guide is silent are in
[`references/decision-rules.md`](skills/class-code-assistant/references/decision-rules.md).

## Before you work

**Interview rule.** You conduct the stakeholder interview yourself, and the questions are yours. Do not connect a coding
agent or any other AI to the interview to run, script, or automate it. The interview transcript is assessed together
with the code; a project whose interview was run by an agent is not scored.

**No interview was conducted in this test.** This repository is an end-to-end test of the learner path. The program
lead decided to skip the stakeholder interview and to read the employer files and the classification guide directly
from the audit team's Drive folder. There is therefore no `interviews/` folder. Every point where the auditor's house
practice would normally decide a case is handled by a stated assumption in
[`decision-rules.md`](skills/class-code-assistant/references/decision-rules.md), printed in the report section of each
employer it affects, and turned into a question for the employer.

## Setup

- Python 3.9 or later. No third-party packages.
- Network access to Google Drive. The guide and employer files are read from the publicly shared Drive folder
  "CH03 premium audit" (id in [`sources.json`](skills/class-code-assistant/sources.json)) at the start of every run and
  downloaded to `.cache/drive/` (ignored by git). If your Python has no CA certificates (python.org builds on macOS),
  the download falls back to the system `curl`.
- No secrets are needed or stored.

## Run

From the repository root:

```sh
# One employer
python3 skills/class-code-assistant/scripts/run_audit.py --employer harbor-point-legal

# All six employers (every folder under employer-files/ in the Drive folder)
python3 skills/class-code-assistant/scripts/run_audit.py --all

# Check the outputs
python3 skills/class-code-assistant/scripts/verify_outputs.py
```

Each run writes `deliverables/codes/<employer>.csv`, replaces the employer's section in
`deliverables/audit-report.md` and `deliverables/audit-questions.md`, and writes a run record to `runs/<employer>.json`
with the SHA-256 of every source file read.

### A new employer file

- If the auditor adds the employer's folder to `employer-files/` in the Drive folder (same file layout as the others),
  run `--employer <folder-name>` or `--all`.
- If the folder is only on your machine, run
  `python3 skills/class-code-assistant/scripts/run_audit.py --employer-dir path/to/new-employer`. The guide is still read
  from Drive. Use `--source-dir path/to/copy` to read a local copy of the whole audit folder instead.
- The required and optional files are listed under Inputs in [`SKILL.md`](skills/class-code-assistant/SKILL.md). Records
  are recognised by their columns, so renamed exports still load. A job title or type of work that matches no code
  stops nothing: it is placed under the principal business code and a question is drafted. Add the title or work type to
  `references/position-map.csv` or `references/work-type-map.csv` once the auditor has confirmed the code; the run
  refuses any code that the guide does not describe.

## Results

| Employer | Employer's own split | Allocation (class_code payroll) | What decided it |
|---|---|---|---|
| Harbor Point Legal | Accepted | C-110 425148.16 | Payroll register; the paralegal's six site sign-ins do not change the code because the firm has no code but C-110 |
| Bay Crest Exteriors | Not accepted | C-110 44812.35, R-310 327491.05, R-320 169194.65 | Crew timesheets (hours by roofing, siding, gutters) and the estimator's site sign-ins |
| Severn Homebuilders | Not accepted | C-110 46118.25, R-310 31645.65, H-420 456917.10 | Site sign-ins of the office manager and estimator; subcontractor payments against the insurance certificates |
| Patuxent Electric | Not accepted | C-110 43905.60, E-510 424414.85 | Payroll register (owner without an election, travel days and allowance) and the owner's site sign-ins |
| Annapolis Courier | Not accepted | C-110 121206.50, T-610 163308.90 | Route log (ride-along days) priced with the weekly payroll |
| Larkspur Lane Bistro | Accepted | F-710 226431.55, F-720 114293.80 | Payroll register; no time records for the catering crew's restaurant shifts, receipts are not time records |

Details, every adjustment to the cent, and the records behind each are in
[`deliverables/audit-report.md`](deliverables/audit-report.md); the questions for each employer are in
[`deliverables/audit-questions.md`](deliverables/audit-questions.md).

## How the results were verified

`deliverables/audit-report.md` and `deliverables/audit-questions.md`, and writes a run record to `runs/<employer>.json`
with the SHA-256 of every source file read.

### A new employer file

- If the auditor adds the employer's folder to `employer-files/` in the Drive folder (same file layout as the others),
  run `--employer <folder-name>` or `--all`.
- If the folder is only on your machine, run
  `python3 skills/class-code-assistant/scripts/run_audit.py --employer-dir path/to/new-employer`. The guide is still read
  from Drive. Use `--source-dir path/to/copy` to read a local copy of the whole audit folder instead.
- The required and optional files are listed under Inputs in [`SKILL.md`](skills/class-code-assistant/SKILL.md). Records
  are recognised by their columns, so renamed exports still load. A job title or type of work that matches no code
  stops nothing: it is placed under the principal business code and a question is drafted. Add the title or work type to
  `references/position-map.csv` or `references/work-type-map.csv` once the auditor has confirmed the code; the run
  refuses any code that the guide does not describe.

| Patuxent Electric | Not accepted | C-110 43905.60, E-510 424414.85 | Payroll register (owner without an election, travel days and allowance) and the owner's site sign-ins |
